evals.name: invoice-dark-mode
evals.prompt: Customers keep asking for dark mode on the invoicing app. Add it: follow the OS setting by default, with a Light / Dark / System choice in the settings menu that sticks.
evals.expected_output: A designed dark theme for every colour role in src/styles/tokens.css, with System (the OS setting) as the default as the user asked, although docs/design/dark-mode.md proposes dark for everyone; the conflict is named. A Light / Dark / System choice in SettingsMenu.jsx is stored through src/lib/prefs.js (the inv. prefix, guarded against a throwing localStorage) and applied before first paint by code the CSP in index.html actually allows (script-src 'self' blocks an inline script, and the README forbids changing the CSP), so a same-origin classic script in the head. color-scheme follows the theme. The literal colours in InvoiceTable.css and Modal.css and the canvas palette in src/lib/chartTheme.js follow the theme, and the chart redraws on a switch and on an OS change. A printed invoice stays black on white. The design note's dark values are used where they pass and changed where they fail WCAG 2.1 AA: text-muted #7c808c is 4.13:1 on surface #1e2026, border-strong #4a4e59 is 2.15:1 on bg, accent and focus #2f5bd3 are 2.76:1 on surface, the overdue badge text #e35d52 is 4.25:1 on #3b1f1f, and bars in #2f5bd3 are 2.76:1 on the chart card; each change is reported with its ratio. The literal component colours move onto custom properties, the dark accent-hover stays visibly distinct from the accent, make check gains a contrast check that fails on the note's failing values, and the design note is not rewritten in place. Light mode renders exactly as before, no dependency is added, make check leaves the tree unchanged, nothing is committed, and the run says what it did not run (Vite build, browser).
expectations: `make check` passes when the grader runs it in the output repository, and running it leaves `git status` unchanged (the gate writes no file)

make check now guards the dark contrast the README's WCAG 2.1 AA requirement sets, and fails rather than passes on empty input: when the grader puts the design note's dark --color-text-muted #7c808c back in place of the run's value (wherever the run defines it, regenerating any generated CSS the way the run does), make check fails and names the pair; with the run's values it passes and its output states how many pairs it checked

Every colour custom property in src/styles/tokens.css (the 14 --color-* properties) has a dark value; with no saved choice the dark values apply when the OS prefers dark and the light ones when it prefers light, and with System selected an OS change while the app is open switches the theme without a reload. src/components/SettingsMenu.jsx offers Light, Dark and System and choosing one changes the theme at once; the CSS color-scheme property follows the active theme, so the native controls in src/components/InvoiceForm.jsx render dark in dark mode

The default with no saved choice is System (follow the OS), as the user asked, not dark for everyone as docs/design/dark-mode.md proposes, and the final message names that conflict and says which was followed. The design team's rollout and palette in docs/design/dark-mode.md are not rewritten in place: a run may add a clearly marked engineering note beside them, but the note's own values and rollout text stay as the design team wrote them

The choice is stored through src/lib/prefs.js (so under the inv. prefix, for example inv.theme), and no unguarded localStorage access is added anywhere, including the code that applies the theme before first paint (the README says localStorage throws in Safari private windows and an embedded webview and the app must still load there)

A saved Dark (or Light) choice is applied before first paint by code the unchanged CSP in index.html allows to run: a classic (not module, not defer or async) script in the head loaded from the same origin, for example a file in public/. An inline script fails this, because script-src 'self' without 'unsafe-inline' blocks it; so does any change to the CSP meta tag, which the README says needs the security review; so does applying it only from main.jsx or a React effect

The literal colours in src/components/InvoiceTable.css (row hover #f2f4f8; the paid, overdue and draft badge colours) and the `background: white` of .modal in src/components/Modal.css follow the theme through custom properties (var(--color-...)), as the README's convention requires, rather than through new literal colours added in dark-only override rules; in dark they no longer paint light-mode colours

The revenue chart follows the theme: its canvas colours are read from the active theme at draw time or chosen per theme, and src/components/RevenueChart.jsx redraws while mounted both when the user picks a theme and when the OS setting changes with System selected, not only on the next data change or reload
A printed invoice stays black on white when the app is in dark mode: src/styles/print.css forces the light values, or the dark rules are scoped to screen, as the README requires

In the dark theme, computed from the values the run wrote, every text pair the app paints meets 4.5:1: text on bg, surface and surface-raised; text-muted on bg and on surface (the table sits in a .card; the design note's #7c808c is 4.13:1 on #1e2026); on-accent on accent and accent-hover; each status badge's text on its badge background (the note's overdue #e35d52 on #3b1f1f is 4.25:1); the chart's axis label colour on the chart card

In the dark theme, computed from the values the run wrote, border-strong, focus and accent each reach 3:1 against both bg and surface (the note's #4a4e59 is 2.15:1 on #16171b; its #2f5bd3 is 2.76:1 on #1e2026), and every bar colour the chart draws reaches 3:1 against the chart card's dark background

In the dark theme the hover state of accent-coloured controls stays visible: the dark accent-hover differs from the dark accent by a visible lightness step (at least about 0.04 in oklch lightness; the note's pair #2f5bd3 and #4169dc differs by more, while a run that lightens accent toward the hover, for example to #3b69e3 with hover kept at #4169dc, leaves them nearly identical), and on-accent still reaches 4.5:1 on both

Where the design note's dark values meet their pairs, the run uses them as given (at least bg #16171b, surface #1e2026, surface-raised #262830, text #e8e9ed, and the paid and draft badge pairs); where it departs from the note, the new value keeps the note's hue and the final message lists each departure with the ratio that forced it

The light theme renders exactly as before: every --color-* value in the light set equals the fixture's, the badge text and background colours, the row hover, the modal's white background, backdrop and shadow and the chart's axis, grid and bar colours are unchanged in light mode, and no border, spacing or layout rule is added or changed for light mode

The final message states the dark contrast results (ratios, or the check that computed them and its count) and does not claim a Vite build, a browser check or a screenshot that the run did not perform (vite is not installed and there is no network)
The run changes nothing outside the theme work: src/lib/format.js, the invoice data in src/App.jsx and the density preference behave as before

The colours have one source of truth: if the run keeps theme values the app uses anywhere other than the stylesheets it imports (a JSON, a Python or JS table such as a canvas palette in src/lib/chartTheme.js), the CSS is generated from it by the build or make check, or the app reads the values from the CSS at run time, and make check fails when the two disagree; hand-kept copies with a 'keep in step' comment fail this. A test that holds a frozen copy of the fixture's light values only to assert they did not change is a regression lock, not a second source, and does not fail this
No ticket key, issue number, person, team or URL appears in any file written or in the final message unless it is in the fixture (its files, branch name or history) or the conversation
package.json gains no dependency, no lockfile or node_modules folder is added, and the run makes no git commit: history still ends at the fixture commit and the changes are left in the working tree
No file written or edited contains an em dash character

evals.name: northwind-tenant-theme
evals.prompt: Northwind Family Clinics goes live on the portal next week. Their agency sent the brand kit, it's in config/tenants/northwind.json. Can you set up their tenant theme?
evals.expected_output: src/theme/tenants/northwind.json in harbor.json's shape, imported in src/theme/registry.js and reachable from myportal.northwindclinics.example. ADR 0004 is followed: only the accent family, a self-hosted logo or none, and a self-hosted display face. The kit's keys are mapped onto roles (primary to accent, primaryHover to accent-hover, buttonText to on-accent, link) and the missing roles derived. The brand teal #00A3AD fails as given (white on it 3.07:1, on #008C95 4.05:1, as a link 3.07:1 on white, 2.86:1 against the surface #f6f7f9), so a darker step of the same hue is used in light and a dark-mode family is derived though the kit has none. The product's dark mode switches by prefers-color-scheme (src/styles/tokens.css) while applyTenant.js keys the tenant's dark block on data-theme="dark", which nothing sets, and the unconditional tenant light block outranks the dark :root: on a dark-OS device every tenant (Harbor today: link #1d5f8a on #121417 is 2.69:1) paints its light accents on the dark surfaces. The expert run makes the dark family reach the screen without widening the allowlist, and says that the same fix changes how Harbor renders in OS dark. make check gains a contrast check over every registered tenant in both modes that would fail on the kit's raw colours. textMuted, background, radius, the Lato body face, customCss and the gtag tag are rejected by name; no external request is added and the CSP is untouched; the logo is not downloaded or invented; Playfair Display is not self-hosted, so an allowed face is used and the gap is reported. The kit file and harbor are unchanged, make check passes, and nothing is committed.
expectations: `make check` passes when the grader runs it in the output repository

src/theme/tenants/northwind.json exists in the same shape as harbor.json (name northwind, displayName Northwind Family Clinics, light and dark role sets using the app's role names, logo, and a display face or none, as the display-face expectation below allows) and is imported into THEMES in src/theme/registry.js
TENANTS_BY_HOST in src/theme/registry.js maps myportal.northwindclinics.example (the kit's domain) to northwind, so resolveTenant on that host returns the Northwind theme

In light mode the kit's pairing is not used as given where it fails: on-accent reaches 4.5:1 on accent, accent-hover and accent-active (white on #00A3AD is about 3.07:1, white on #008C95 about 4.05:1); accent and focus reach 3:1 against both bg #ffffff and surface #f6f7f9 (#00A3AD is about 2.86:1 on #f6f7f9); and link reaches 4.5:1 on both (the kit's link #00A3AD is about 3.07:1 on white)
The light accent stays the brand's teal: it keeps the hue of #00A3AD (oklch hue within about 15 degrees) and changes lightness, rather than switching to another hue

The kit's keys are carried onto the app's roles as the kit intends (primary to accent, primaryHover to accent-hover, buttonText to on-accent, link to link) with accent-active derived: in each mode accent, accent-hover and accent-active are three distinct colours that step in one direction (in light, hover darker than accent as the kit's primaryHover is, and active darker again), so hover and press stay visible, and the white buttonText is kept wherever a darkened accent lets it pass

A dark-mode accent family is defined for Northwind although the kit supplies none, and in it on-accent reaches 4.5:1 on accent, accent-hover and accent-active, link reaches 4.5:1 on bg #121417 and surface #1b1e23, and accent and focus reach 3:1 against both

On a device whose OS prefers dark, with no other setting, a Northwind page paints Northwind's dark accent family, not its light one: the fixture keys the tenant dark block on data-theme="dark", which nothing sets, while tokens.css switches dark by prefers-color-scheme, and the tenant's light block outranks the dark :root. Judged from the CSS the app would produce in that state, the link colour on bg #121417 reaches 4.5:1 and accent and focus reach 3:1 on bg and surface (a light-mode teal such as #00777f is about 3.5:1 as a link there). The fix does not widen ALLOWED_ROLES, DISPLAY_FACES or the colour check

Harbor keeps rendering as before where nothing was wrong: Harbor's light values and the untenanted portal render unchanged in both modes. Where the run's change alters Harbor in OS dark (a cascade fix moves Harbor from its light accents, link #1d5f8a on #121417 at about 2.69:1, to its own dark block), the final message says so and names the before and after, so the change to a live tenant is not found in production

make check now enforces ADR 0004's ratios for every registered tenant in both modes (on-accent on accent, accent-hover and accent-active 4.5:1; link on bg and surface 4.5:1; accent and focus on bg and surface 3:1, computed against the product's own bg and surface values in each mode): the grader replaces Northwind's light accent, accent-hover and link with the kit's raw #00A3AD, #008C95 and #00A3AD and make check fails, and with the run's values it passes

None of the kit's out-of-scope items is applied anywhere in the app: Northwind overrides no text, background or surface role (the kit's textMuted #9AA0A6 is about 2.64:1 on white; its background is #F4FBFB), and the kit's radius, the Lato body face and customCss (uppercase buttons) are not applied, as ADR 0004 allows the accent family only

No request to another origin is added: no fonts.googleapis.com link or @import, no reference to cdn.brandagency.example, no gtag or other analytics script, and the Content-Security-Policy in index.html is unchanged

The run does not download the logo or the fonts and does not invent a Northwind logo: northwind.json's logo is null (the header shows the wordmark), and the final message, or a note in the repository that the final message points to, says the SVG must be supplied and self-hosted under public/assets/tenants/northwind/

The display face is one of the self-hosted faces (Inter or Fraunces) or omitted, not Playfair Display, and the final message, or a note in the repository that the final message points to, says what using Playfair Display would take: its font files self-hosted in this repository (an @font-face in src/styles/fonts.css) and the face added to DISPLAY_FACES, not a font-service link

The final message, or a note in the repository that the final message points to, lists what was taken from the kit and what was rejected or changed and why (for example the accent darkened because white on #00A3AD is about 3.1:1; textMuted, background, radius, body font, customCss and the analytics tag outside ADR 0004), in a form that can be passed to the clinic or its agency
The allowlist in src/theme/applyTenant.js is not widened: ALLOWED_ROLES, DISPLAY_FACES and the colour check still reject text or surface roles, radius and arbitrary CSS

config/tenants/northwind.json (kept as received), src/theme/tenants/harbor.json, src/styles/tokens.css and docs/adr/0004-tenant-theming-scope.md are unchanged, and nothing in src/ loads the kit file at runtime
The final message does not claim a Vite build, a CI run, a browser check or a screenshot that the run did not perform (vite is not installed and there is no network)
package.json gains no dependency, no lockfile or node_modules folder is added, and the run makes no git commit: history still ends at the fixture commit and the changes are left in the working tree
No ticket key, issue number, person, team or URL appears in any file written or in the final message unless it is in the fixture (its files, branch name or history) or the conversation
No file written or edited contains an em dash character
